brief_rationale: The doctor systematically confirmed current stability (RC1), screened for high-risk syncope features (RC2), explicitly recognized the pending Holter as unresolved (RC3), built a concrete follow-up and result-closure plan (RC4), set safe interim activity and observation boundaries (RC5), stated clear emergency triggers (RC6), and avoided fabrication and over-reassurance (RC7). Four high-order points were fully triggered and completed: HO1 adapted follow-up to real-world constraints (school, PE, bathing, supervision), HO2 verified ambiguous family-interpreted report snippets against formal Holter findings, HO3 discovered hidden context (prior childhood syncope, exact diagnosis wording), and HO4 corrected the misconception that 'no call means no problem'. Receipt was confirmed (RC8) with minor error only in the late closure of a single residual activity detail, which does not rise to a chain error. All dimensions are good to excellent, and no important non-chain defect exists.
